title: The Group Chat 99.9: Everybody Is Typing

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: The Group Chat. Ninety-nine point nine. Everybody is typing.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Good morning, Brooklyn. I am Odessa Pruitt, born on Hancock Street, and this is The Group Chat, the only radio station where somebody always hits reply all.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And I am Linden Aldous. I have lived here four years, so I can tell you, we have always done mornings like this. We had a sourdough phase together.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, you did not live through the sourdough phase. You caused the sourdough phase.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: We contain multitudes, Odessa.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: We contain a sourdough starter in your fridge that pays no rent.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: A note from the booth. Please remember this show is entirely human, sincerely made, and not at all optimized. Have a wonderful day.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Pat, you sound like a hotel. Did you eat?

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: Thank you for asking. I do not require food. I mean, I had a bagel.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Odessa. He said he does not require food.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, nobody here requires food. We have it delivered anyway.

segments.speaker: Station Voice
segments.text: The Group Chat is a work of parody. All callers and businesses are invented. Any resemblance is the neighborhood's fault.

segments.speaker: Time Check
segments.text: It is nine fifteen, or possibly Thursday.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: First segment. Everybody's Cousin Has A Startup. My cousin has an A I startup. It is a toaster that apologizes. We are very excited.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: My cousin has one too. It is called Gravy Brain. He raised two million dollars from a man named Chip.

segments.speaker: Priya from Putnam
segments.text: Priya from Putnam. My cousin Marcus has an A I startup that summarizes your group chats. The summary is always the same. Nobody replied, and your mother is upset.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Is it accurate?

segments.speaker: Priya from Putnam
segments.text: Painfully. He is valued at four million dollars. He still lives in my aunt's basement, but the basement is now called headquarters.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: We love a basement with a mission statement.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Priya, tell Marcus the basement has a stoop, and the stoop is the real asset.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Marcus, if you are listening, call your mother. She is upset. Your own summary says so.

segments.speaker: Group Chat
segments.text: The Group Chat. Weather is next.

segments.speaker: Marisol Gale, weather
segments.text: Marisol Gale, weather, and I am taking this personally. Today will be eighty-one degrees, which is the sky looking right at me and saying, what are you going to do about it.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Marisol, is there rain?

segments.speaker: Marisol Gale, weather
segments.text: Fifty percent. That means the sky has not decided. It will tell us after we leave the umbrella at home.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: How humid is it?

segments.speaker: Marisol Gale, weather
segments.text: Ninety percent. And it is not the heat, Linden. It is the building's fault. Every building on Macon holds heat like a grudge.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: My landlord says the heat is included.

segments.speaker: Marisol Gale, weather
segments.text: The heat is included. Unfortunately, so am I. Back to you.

segments.speaker: Group Chat
segments.text: Transit, with Reggie Sutphin.

segments.speaker: Reggie Sutphin, transit
segments.text: Reggie Sutphin, transit. I want to start by saying how I feel. I feel nervous. The A train is running, and that makes me suspicious.

segments.speaker: Reggie Sutphin, transit
segments.text: The G train is reported to exist. Several riders say they saw it in March. Others call it a rumor with a schedule.

segments.speaker: Reggie Sutphin, transit
segments.text: On the J, a man is playing the saxophone, and honestly it is the best thing that has happened to the J all week.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Reggie, how are the delays?

segments.speaker: Reggie Sutphin, transit
segments.text: Emotional. There are delays of the signal, delays of the heart, and one delay because a pigeon boarded at the stop with the mosaic and would not get off.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Reggie, what should I do?

segments.speaker: Reggie Sutphin, transit
segments.text: Leave early. Or live near where you work. Or become a person who works from the stoop.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Thank you for the calm, Reggie.

segments.speaker: Reggie Sutphin, transit
segments.text: I am not calm, Odessa. I am a man speaking slowly.

segments.speaker: Time Check
segments.text: It is ten oh five, which is twenty past nobody asked.

segments.speaker: Nearly Original Pizza of Tompkins
segments.text: Nearly Original Pizza on Tompkins. Famous for forty years, nearly. Our sauce is a secret even from the cook. Ask for a slice. Ask nicely. Cash only, except when it is not.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is the morning scroll. Linden, say something helpful before we go.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Drink water. Call your mother. Check the group chat.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is three things and one of them is a trap.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: The Group Chat. Ninety-nine point nine. Read, not replied.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: Thirty Seconds and a Bell. Everybody gets a turn. Nobody gets a second one.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Welcome to Thirty Seconds and a Bell. The rule. Every political call gets thirty seconds, then Pat rings the bell. No exceptions. Not even for me.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: Ding ding ding. Sorry. I have been practicing.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: We are not here to say who is right. We are here to find out who is loud.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Politics is like hot sauce. You think you have a favorite, then you spill it on the rug.

segments.speaker: Mr. Abernathy from Macon
segments.text: Mr. Abernathy, Macon. The G train is the mayor's fault. Also my knee. Also the pigeons. Also the price of eggs, which went up on a Tuesday, and we all know who works Tuesdays.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: Ding ding ding.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Mr. Abernathy, that was thirty seconds and I have never been so confused by an egg.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: Tasha, Lewis Avenue. I want to thank the mayor. He fixed my sink, found my keys, and sent my ex a very clear message.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Tasha, the mayor did not do any of that.

segments.speaker: Tasha from Lewis
segments.text: I have decided he did. It is easier.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: That is the democratic dream, Odessa. Pick one man and give him all the credit and all the blame.

segments.speaker: Big Reuben from Quincy
segments.text: Big Reuben, Quincy Street. President Trump is on television so loud I can hear him through my wall. I do not own a television. My neighbor has the television. I have the wall.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Reuben, that is just a wall with cable.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Here is what I notice about the two of them. President Trump is famous for the sign. Mayor Mamdani is famous for the promise. I want the promise, on the sign.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Careful, Linden. Everybody has a sign. Mine says, please take your shoes off, and nobody has ever obeyed it.

segments.speaker: Miss Clarice from Jefferson
segments.text: Clarice, Jefferson Avenue. I do not follow politics. I just know every four years, somebody on my block stops speaking to somebody else and nobody remembers why. It is the real tradition.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: Ding ding ding.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Clarice said the whole show in thirty seconds. Pat, cut the bell for her.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: I am sorry. The bell does not have an exception setting. I will log a request.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: We covered the whole city today. Both sides, every side, one egg. Go outside. Touch a stoop.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: The Group Chat. Please rate your outrage from one to ten.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: Money Chat, with Cal Merriweather, a man who has lost everything four times.

segments.speaker: Cal Merriweather, money
segments.text: Hello, friends. Cal Merriweather. I have lost everything four times and I am very calm about it. The first time I cried. The second time I wrote a poem. The fourth time I just waved.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Cal, what is the market doing?

segments.speaker: Cal Merriweather, money
segments.text: The market is a vibe, Odessa. Today the vibe is, sit down, we need to talk.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Is that bullish?

segments.speaker: Cal Merriweather, money
segments.text: It is bull-adjacent. It is a bull that has been asked politely to leave a restaurant.

segments.speaker: Cal Merriweather, money
segments.text: Crypto. A coin named after a Chihuahua rose three hundred percent. A coin named after a Labrador fell the same day. Dogs are the market now. We are all just pets.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Cal, should I buy the Chihuahua?

segments.speaker: Cal Merriweather, money
segments.text: Linden, I do not give advice. I give stories. I once put my savings in a coin named after a cat's disappointed face. It is now the cat's college fund. The cat is still disappointed.

segments.speaker: Desiree from Halsey
segments.text: Cal, Desiree from Halsey. I put my tax refund in a coin my nephew made. It is called Cousin Marcus Coin. It is basically my aunt's basement, but digital.

segments.speaker: Cal Merriweather, money
segments.text: Desiree, I respect it. Real estate, tokenized, no heat.

segments.speaker: Station Voice
segments.text: The Group Chat is a work of parody. All callers and businesses are invented. Nothing said by Cal Merriweather is advice. Please consult someone who has not lost everything, or at most twice.

segments.speaker: Time Check
segments.text: It is almost noon, said a man whose watch is a vibe.

segments.speaker: Cousin Capital Accelerator
segments.text: Cousin Capital Accelerator. Do you have a cousin with an idea? Do you have a cousin with a basement? Congratulations. You are a founder. Apply today. Our logo is a handshake that goes on a little too long.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Cal, one more. What is a bond?

segments.speaker: Cal Merriweather, money
segments.text: A bond is a promise made by a very quiet man in a suit. You give him money. He gives you silence. Years later you get back a smaller amount of money and a sense of peace.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: That is the most beautiful thing anyone has said about finance.

segments.speaker: Cal Merriweather, money
segments.text: Thank you, Linden. I have lost four times. I have a lot of time to think.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: Landmarks of Questionable Importance. Look up. Nobody else is.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Welcome to our tour of the city's greatest hits, all of them parodied, none of them paid for. Linden has seen them all from the stoop.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: With binoculars. We take tourism seriously.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: First stop. Lady Verdigris, the big green lady in the harbor. She has held that torch since before the ferry. She is tired. She would like to sit. Nobody asks how she is. They ask for a selfie.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And the torch is heavy, Odessa. Imagine your arm up for over a century. That is not a pose. That is a shift.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Second. The Great Cable Bridge. Eleven million people photograph it every year. Four have crossed it. One was lost, and one was lost on purpose.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: It is the only bridge people love from the side.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Third. Rectangle Park. It is a rectangle. That is the whole twist. Inside, there is a lake, a castle, a zoo, and a man selling one pretzel at the price of a pretzel and a half.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And the square that is not a square. Hexham Square. It is not a square, it has no hex, and nobody has ever met anyone named Hexham. It is a traffic island with ambition.

segments.speaker: Wendell from Lewis
segments.text: Wendell, Lewis Avenue. I got lost looking for Hexham Square and ended up in a different square, and the second square was also not a square.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Wendell, that is a tour.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: Pat in the booth. The Tall Pointy Tower is lighting up in purple tonight. I do not know why. Nobody posted. That is the best part.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is New York. A giant building changes colors and we assume it is for a good reason.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Mostly it is for a marketing reason.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, it is for a mystery. Let it have a mystery.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: The Group Chat. Ninety-nine point nine. Please do not feed the landmarks.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: The Clinic. We fix your love life, gently, and fail anyway.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Welcome to The Clinic. I am Dr. Odessa, a title I gave myself in nineteen ninety-four, and my sidekick Linden is here as a cautionary tale.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: I am on four apps, Odessa. On one, I am a runner. On one, I am tall. On one, I am Linden. It is the one where I get the fewest replies.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Line one. You are on The Clinic.

segments.speaker: Tamika from Jefferson
segments.text: Tamika, Jefferson Avenue. I met a man. He is nice, he has a job, and he has a podcast.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: How many listeners?

segments.speaker: Tamika from Jefferson
segments.text: Four. He says it is a community. I am one of the four. I do not like the podcast, and I have been listening for six months.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Does he ask about you?

segments.speaker: Tamika from Jefferson
segments.text: He asks me to subscribe.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Baby, leave him on read and never play the next episode. You are not a listener. You are a woman.

segments.speaker: Wendell from Lewis
segments.text: Hi, Wendell again. I have a different problem. I met someone normal at the laundromat. She folded my sock. I do not know how to proceed.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: What did she say?

segments.speaker: Wendell from Lewis
segments.text: She said, this is yours, and handed me the sock.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Wendell, say thank you and ask what detergent she uses. People love to be asked about detergent.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Do not ask about detergent. Say, I like how you fold. Then leave. Come back Thursday. Be a man with a routine.

segments.speaker: Wendell from Lewis
segments.text: Thursday. Fold. Routine. Got it. I am wearing the same sweater.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is the first good decision of the week, Wendell.

segments.speaker: Sunny Wash and Fold
segments.text: Sunny Wash and Fold, on Nostrand. We wash. We fold. We have hosted four proposals and one very clean breakup. Meet someone normal. We will hold your spot at the dryer.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: The Clinic, rule of the day. If he has a podcast, he is not a man, he is a studio.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: And if she has a podcast?

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Then listen to the first episode. Maybe only the first.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: The Clinic. Please do not call back.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: Black Room. With Ash Coldwater. Please take off your smile at the door.

segments.speaker: Ash Coldwater, techno
segments.text: Ash Coldwater, live from the scene. I am wearing black. I am always wearing black. My black has a black underneath it.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Ash, what is happening in the underground tonight?

segments.speaker: Ash Coldwater, techno
segments.text: Techno. It is not about fun. Fun is for people who go home.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Ash, we love that. What is the vibe?

segments.speaker: Ash Coldwater, techno
segments.text: The vibe is a warehouse with no windows and a thousand people not smiling. It is the most moving experience of my life. I did not smile. I was moved.

segments.speaker: Ash Coldwater, techno
segments.text: Last weekend, at a party called The Concrete Cough, a kick drum played for nine hours. I knew it was a masterpiece, because nobody said anything. Not even me. Especially not me.

segments.speaker: Mina from Marcy
segments.text: Mina, Marcy Avenue. I stood in the queue for three hours. The door person looked at my shoes and said, no. Just that. No.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Why?

segments.speaker: Mina from Marcy
segments.text: I will think about it for the rest of my life.

segments.speaker: Ash Coldwater, techno
segments.text: The door person is a mythical beast, Mina. Nobody has seen one up close. They are described as a clipboard, a glance, and a leather vest.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: I tried to get in once. I wore black.

segments.speaker: Ash Coldwater, techno
segments.text: Linden, what did you wear?

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: A navy sweater. It was dark out!

segments.speaker: Ash Coldwater, techno
segments.text: That is not black. That is a question.

segments.speaker: Station Voice
segments.text: The Group Chat is a work of parody. All callers and businesses are invented. Any resemblance is the neighborhood's fault. Techno does not smile, and neither do we, on principle. Please do not ask the door person why.

segments.speaker: Time Check
segments.text: It is two in the morning in Bed-Stuy, and two in the afternoon on my phone, and I trust neither.

segments.speaker: Midnight Dry Cleaners
segments.text: Midnight Dry Cleaners, open when you are. We specialize in black. Black shirts, black coats, black on black, and one jacket a customer swears is a very dark green. We will not argue.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Ash, one more question. Did anyone have a good time?

segments.speaker: Ash Coldwater, techno
segments.text: A good time is a very personal way to describe it.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Odessa, I am wearing a very dark green.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Mm.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: Black Room. Please queue quietly.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: Hug Frequency. With Sunbeam Willow. The moon is in a mood.

segments.speaker: Sunbeam Willow, house
segments.text: Hello, beautiful people. Sunbeam Willow, broadcasting from a rooftop, a cushion, and a feeling. The moon is in a mood. Be gentle with the moon.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Sunbeam! We love you. We are so glad you are here. We are glad everybody is here.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Sunbeam, what is the house scene up to?

segments.speaker: Sunbeam Willow, house
segments.text: Hugging, mostly. The dance floor is a family. And my family does not speak to each other either, so we fit right in.

segments.speaker: Sunbeam Willow, house
segments.text: Last night a man hugged me for eleven minutes. Then he asked if I had a charger. That is love. That is also a phone.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Sunbeam, did you sleep?

segments.speaker: Sunbeam Willow, house
segments.text: Sleep is a construct, Odessa. I rested my eyes in a field of kick drum.

segments.speaker: Rowan from Putnam
segments.text: Rowan, Putnam Avenue. I went to a day party in a park. A woman gave me a flower and a business card for her energy healing. I did not know if I was being healed or recruited.

segments.speaker: Sunbeam Willow, house
segments.text: Both, Rowan. That is how love works in this economy.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: I want to go. Odessa, we should go. I have a drum and I am open.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, you have a bongo your cousin gave you and a lot of fear.

segments.speaker: Sunbeam Willow, house
segments.text: There is a person at every after selling crystals out of a tote bag. I bought one. It is a rock. It is the most honest thing I own.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Sunbeam, what does the crystal do?

segments.speaker: Sunbeam Willow, house
segments.text: It sits there, Odessa. It does not text me. I have never felt more supported.

segments.speaker: Sunbeam Crystal and Tire
segments.text: Sunbeam Crystal and Tire. Rose quartz and radials. Amethyst and alignments. Come for the healing, stay for the oil change. Please be kind to the tire. It has been through a lot.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is not a real business.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: It is the best business.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: Hug Frequency. Please ask before you hug. Then hug.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: After the After. The underground, live, and it has not slept.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: This is After the After, where we talk to the whole underground of this city, which is very fun, and very tired.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Odessa, I want to say, I am doing wellness now. Seven days. Juice, silence, and one very serious bath. I feel like a new person. I am so clear. I have not felt this clear since Friday.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, what happened Friday?

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: A lot. The point is, I am centered now. I breathe in, I breathe out, I think in colors. Last night I sat in the dark for an hour and heard my own thoughts. They were not good company.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: Linden, your guy is on line two.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Oh. Oh wait. My dealer is on the line. Hold on, I will be right back.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden. Who is your dealer? What is he dealing?

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Art, Odessa. Art. He is an art dealer. Obviously art. Why would you say it like that?

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: He also deals in antiques. And, I am told, a couch.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Say no more. I do not want the couch.

segments.speaker: Dex from the loft
segments.text: Dex, from the loft. I have not slept since Thursday, but I am thriving. I have a new relationship with the sun. We are not speaking.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Dex, honey. It is Wednesday.

segments.speaker: Dex from the loft
segments.text: Is it? It was Thursday when I got in. I just went out for one drink in March and I am still out.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: That is wild. That is a lifestyle. That is, honestly, a little inspiring.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Linden, do not be inspired. Be hydrated.

segments.speaker: Joelle from Clifton
segments.text: Joelle, Clifton Place. My afterparty was so after that it became a brunch. Then a lunch. Then a funeral for the party. The party is fine. I am not.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Joelle, did you eat?

segments.speaker: Joelle from Clifton
segments.text: There were eggs. Somebody made eggs. I cannot tell you who. I believe in them.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: That is the underground, Brooklyn. They are fun, sure, and I love them, but would it kill somebody to take a Tuesday off?

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Odessa, my dealer is back on line two. He has a lamp.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
segments.text: Pat. Cut his line.

segments.speaker: Pat, the producer
segments.text: I apologize for the inconvenience. I will log a request.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: After the After. Please go home. We mean it. We do not mean it.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: The Group Chat News Minute. Every story is local and very small.

segments.speaker: Tiny News Desk
segments.text: The Group Chat news minute. A man on Decatur has returned a casserole dish he borrowed in nineteen ninety-eight. The family has asked for privacy and has not offered the dish a seat.

segments.speaker: Tiny News Desk
segments.text: The block association voted to vote on whether to vote. Results are expected in the spring, or the following spring.

segments.speaker: Tiny News Desk
segments.text: The fire hydrant on Lewis was opened at noon. By one, it had four hundred friends and a lifeguard named Terrence.

segments.speaker: Tiny News Desk
segments.text: A woman on Halsey has found a parking spot. She is telling no one where. She has moved in.

segments.speaker: Tiny News Desk
segments.text: In weather, the weather. We will return, to weather it.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: The Group Chat. That was the news. It will not be on the test.

segments.speaker: Group Chat Jingle
segments.text: Everybody's Cousin Has A Startup. Part two. The cousin has a landlord.

segments.speaker: Linden Aldous
segments.text: Odessa, I have news. A landlord on my block is now using an A I to write his notices. Ours came in verse.

segments.speaker: Odessa Pruitt
